details.description: moonshot-v1-auto was the "auto-router" chat model in Moonshot AI's original moonshot-v1 line, alongside the fixed context-length variants moonshot-v1-8k, moonshot-v1-32k and moonshot-v1-128k; it was launched in August 2024. Moonshot AI (whose developer platform now operates as Kimi) closed the moonshot-v1 series to newly registered users in July 2026 when it launched its current flagship, Kimi K3, and fully retired the series platform-wide on August 31, 2026, after which calls to moonshot-v1-auto return a 404 "model not found" error. Moonshot AI directs remaining users to migrate to kimi-k3.
advantages: As the "auto-router" entry in Moonshot's list-models API, it sat alongside the 8K/32K/128K moonshot-v1 tiers, reaching up to the series' 128K-token top tier.
disadvantages: Fully retired by Moonshot AI on August 31, 2026; API calls to this model now return a 404 "model not found" error.
Was already closed to newly registered accounts from July 2026, before the full retirement.
Text-only: Moonshot offered vision input only through separate moonshot-v1-*-vision-preview models (also retired), not this one.
Superseded by Moonshot AI's current flagship, kimi-k3, which the maker recommends migrating to.
use_cases: General-purpose text chat completions via Moonshot's Chat Completions API, for existing accounts that already had access before the series closed to new sign-ups.

sources.title: Platform Changelog — Kimi Open Platform (Moonshot AI)

notes: Moonshot AI's developer platform now redirects platform.moonshot.ai -> platform.kimi.ai (rebrand to 'Kimi'). Current docs list moonshot-v1-auto only as a retired entry and never explain the mechanics of how 'auto' picked among the 8k/32k/128k tiers, so that selection behavior is not stated here (dropped rather than guessed from memory). The catalog's facts (131072 max input/output tokens, text-only, /v1/chat/completions) are consistent with what the sources describe. Given the confirmed August 31, 2026 platform-wide retirement (calls now 404), Bud may want to consider whether this model should still be offered at all.
